messages:
maya: Nightly e2e failed the throughput gate for longseq tests (p95 ~ 1.8s vs baseline 1.1s). Can someone kick a rerun? We need to know if it's a flake or real regression.
ci-bot: [alert] nightly-e2e (longseq) — throughput_gate: FAILED — p95: 1.83s — baseline: 1.10s — job id: #nightly-20260317-42
jon: I can grab this. Any quick logs pointing at batcher or kvcache?
maya: Early look shows the batcher wait metric spiked. There's a few timeouts in runner logs: `ERROR: kvcache: timeout fetching prefix for request 0x1f4` and `batcher: flush latency 480ms`.
priya: Can we rerun the same job with --collect-profiling to capture scheduler traces? If it's noisy we'll need trace.
maya: @jon please rerun with profiling. Command we usually use: `/rerun nightly-e2e --job longseq --collect-profiling`
jon: doing it now. queued the rerun.
ci-bot: Rerun queued: nightly-e2e longseq — job id #nightly-20260317-42-rerun1 — started.
liam: FYI, we've been rolling kernel updates on canary infra; could affect network/batcher timers. Ping infra if rerun also fails.
jon: Quick status after rerun: preliminary p95 1.12s, looks close to baseline. But one shard still had a 1.7s tail.
maya: Hmm. Mixed results — could be an intermittent scheduling issue or a particular commit. Suggest a bisect across last deploys: bisect range commit A -> commit D (last 4 commits).
priya: I can run a 2-phase bisect: first narrow down suspected commit window, then run targeted longseq. Assigning to @priya.
maya: Thanks. Also saving the profiler: /artifacts/nightly-20260317-42-rerun1/profiler.tar.gz
jon: If bisect shows noise, we should run with pinned kernels (previous kernel version) to rule infra. Filing infra ticket now: #INC-3248
liam: Noted, I'll coordinate with infra on kernel pins and ETA.
priya: Starting bisect job now. Will post updates every step. :white_check_mark:
maya: Awesome — if anyone sees a fast remediation (e.g., revert recent scheduling tweak), mention here before we escalate.
ci-bot: Bisect job started: bisect-20260317-1 — monitoring.
jon: thanks all, will follow up when bisect narrows it down.
